transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm here because I've been struggling with really severe, exhausting mood swings for the past nine months. I keep alternating between periods of overwhelming energy and racing thoughts, and times of deep depression where I lose all my motivation. It has just become too much to handle on my own.
Have you ever had times when you heard or saw things that other people did not, or had strong beliefs that others said were not true?

Yes, I have experienced both of those, but it only happens during the phases when my energy is incredibly high. I've heard voices and seen things that weren't there, and I became convinced that I was being watched or that I had special, extraordinary powers. These experiences completely fade away once that intense energy level drops.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Bipolar I Disorder, Bipolar II Disorder, Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features, Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)], but the new information shows hallucinations and delusional beliefs occur only during the periods of elevated mood/energy and fully resolve when the mood episode ends. That pattern supports bipolar I disorder with psychotic features and makes schizoaffective disorder less likely because psychosis is not occurring outside mood episodes. Bipolar II disorder is also unlikely because there are clear psychotic symptoms during high-energy episodes, which indicates mania rather than hypomania.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes recurrent episodes of markedly elevated energy with racing thoughts consistent with mania, alternating with depressive periods over 9 months. Psychotic symptoms (auditory/visual hallucinations and grandiose/paranoid delusions) occur only during the high-energy phases and resolve when mood normalizes, which supports bipolar I disorder with psychotic features rather than schizoaffective disorder or a primary psychotic disorder.
